arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Blatt argued the relevant conduct is the facts asserted in the original habeas grounds.
She stated this reference point preserves Congress' intent to accelerate habeas proceedings.
Mr. Chan argued Congress made an important change to habeas proceedings in 1996.
He noted the Court is asked to consider the relation back doctrine for the first time in this context.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests how courts apply the relation back doctrine to habeas petitions. The core dispute involves the one-year statute of limitations under AEDPA. the sides that brought the case want to add new claims to their existing petition. the opposing sides want the court to reject the new claims as time-barred. The Court must decide if the new claims relate back to the original filing date.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of the one-year habeas deadline. It determines whether prisoners can add new claims to old petitions. The outcome shapes the finality of state court judgments. It balances the need for prompt resolution against the right to seek relief.
